name: MRF Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest tyre maker by value (Rs 31,900 cr TTM sales): passenger, truck/bus, two-wheeler, off-the-road and aircraft tyres plus MRF Pro-Racing/ toys/ paints. Replacement ~60%, OEM ~30%, exports ~10% of revenue. Highest-priced Indian stock (about Rs 1.25 lakh per share). Natural and synthetic rubber, carbon black, nylon and steel cord are ~67% of sales, so margins track rubber and crude-derivative prices with a lag of two to three quarters. Promoter holding 27.6%; FIIs 17.1%.

cost_structure.note: natural + synthetic as % of sales, model estimate (Mint: rubber ~ half of tyre cost)
carbon black, nylon, chemicals as % of sales, model estimate

exposures.mechanism: Raw materials ~67% of sales (Q1 gross margin 32.7%). Natural + synthetic rubber ~45% of RM = ~30% of sales (Mint: rubber is about half of tyre manufacturing cost). +10% rubber -> +3.0% of sales cost; EBITDA margin ~13% (Q1 12%) -> -23% EBITDA pre pass-through; ~60% recovered in 2-3 qtrs (MRF has lagged peers' hikes) -> -9.2%; EV/MCap ~1.03; persistence 0.35 -> -3.3. RSS4 is +62% y/y to Rs 300/kg, so most of the shock is already in H1 costs; further rise is the risk.

evidence.note: RSS4 rubber +62% to Rs 300/kg vs Nov 2025; rubber ~half of tyre cost; CEAT EBITDA -11%, JK EBITDA -36% in Sept quarter
Q1 gross margin down 570bp q/q to 32.7%; MRF price hikes lag peers; Anand Rathi sees 8-10% RM basket rise in Q2

exposures.mechanism: Crude derivatives not captured in the rubber edge (carbon black, nylon cord, chemicals, freight) ~14% of sales; +10% Brent -> +4% on these -> +0.56% of sales -> -4.3% EBITDA pre; 40% pass-through -> -2.6%; x1.03 x0.35 = -0.95. Matches pack empirical -0.92 per +10% (t -2.4). Brent ~$95 today (factor_state) after a 6-month high late October (reports of ~$112 on 2 Nov, Upstox; sources conflict).

evidence.note: Brent ended October at its highest in six months; Iran-Qatar talks on ending the war

exposures.mechanism: Carbon black feedstock (FCC/CBFS) and aromatic oils follow refinery by-product prices; empirical -1.04 per +$2/bbl GRM (t -2.9) is mostly the same crude regime as the Brent edge. Weight shrunk to avoid double counting.
Steel cord/bead wire ~4% of sales; +7% -> 0.28% of sales -> -2.2% EBITDA pre; 60% recovered -> -0.9%; x1.03 x0.35 = -0.3 plus pass lag -> -0.5.

evidence.note: Rubber, carbon black, chemicals, silica and steel all inflating tyre costs

exposures.mechanism: Net import-long: imported natural rubber, carbon black, nylon, steel cord ~25% of sales vs exports ~8% -> net 17% of sales USD-linked. +3% -> +0.5% of sales -> -3.9% EBITDA pre; 40% hedged/passed -> -2.3%; x1.03 x0.35 = -0.85, upward to -1.2 for domestic rubber price following parity. Pack empirical -1.55 per +3% (t -1.4) consistent in sign. INR is 94.5, -1.1% since June.

OEM (PV, CV, 2W) ~30% of revenue; replacement ~60%; exports ~10%. +10% auto volumes -> OEM tyre sales +10% = +3% of revenue at lower margin (contribution ~20% vs 13% EBITDA) -> EBITDA +4.6%; x1.03 x0.3 = +1.4. Record Oct industry PV sales (>5 lakh) and strong OE demand are giving tyre makers room to pass on costs (Mint).

evidence.note: Strong demand from automakers gives tyre makers room to pass on costs

exposures.mechanism: Replacement truck/bus and passenger tyres track freight and consumption: +1pp GDP -> +0.7pp volume -> EBITDA +1.5% (gearing ~2.2x on 0.7%) x1.03 x0.6 persistence = +0.9 -> 1.0. RBI projects FY27 GDP 7.1%.

Debt is modest (interest Rs 356 cr/yr on ~Rs 4.5k cr, offset by ~Rs 3k cr treasury) so direct interest sensitivity is small (+25bp = ~Rs 5 cr); effect is mostly multiple compression and weaker CV/replacement demand: -0.6. Hike to 5.50% on 2026-10-07.

Chinese truck-bus radial and passenger tyre imports compete with domestic tyres; new broad duties (+1) -> import share -2pp -> volume +1.5% for MRF's CV/TBR-heavy mix -> EBITDA +3% x1.03 x0.2 ... +0.6. No specific 2026 action verified.

Imported inputs ~25% of sales; freight ~5% of landed cost -> +25% freight = +1.25% of import cost = 0.3% of sales -> -2.3% EBITDA pre; recovered 50%; x1.03 x0.35 = -0.4; Red Sea/Gulf disruptions already in rates -> -0.3.

evidence.note: Supply-chain constraints from West Asia crisis cited by JK Tyre CFO (raw material +30% in six months)

supply_chain.counterparty: Natural rubber growers/importers (Rubber Board, SE Asia)

supply_chain.note: raising prices faster than MRF; CEAT Q2 PAT -40%, JK PAT -73%

supply_chain.counterparty: Maruti Suzuki, M&M, Tata, Hero (OEM customers)

GST on retreaded tractor tyres cut to 5% (effective); minor positive for tractor/replacement segments

current_state.trend: Q1: standalone revenue Rs 8,292 cr (+10%), EBITDA Rs 949 cr (-8%), gross margin 32.7% (-570bp q/q), adjusted PAT Rs 474 cr (-2%, aided by +53% other income). Peers' Sept quarter: CEAT EBITDA -11%/PAT -40%; JK Tyre EBITDA -36%/PAT -73%. Anand Rathi expected MRF's RM basket +8-10% in Q2.
current_state.valuation: Rs 1,24,900, market cap Rs 52.9k cr, P/E 21.5x (below its 5-year average), near 52-wk low (Rs 1,15,190 low, Rs 1,59,800 high); -20.9% over 12 months; hit 52-week low on 2026-10-21.

Weak CV demand after festive season; RBI tightening
